title: Planner-statless SQLite was the root cause of bb_graph 15-20s and bb_patterns 45s+ timeouts

rootCause.statement: sqlite_stat1 did not exist in any real brain.db (ANALYZE was never run). SQLite's planner therefore chose brain_symbol_project_idx for the graph owner-cascade member scan (owner_symbol_id >= ? AND < ?), scanning every project symbol per traversal hop.
rootCause.discovery: strace on the spawned MCP server showed the DB actually opened; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN showed the bad index choice; --cpu-prof on the server attributed 43.1s of 46.7s sampled to SQLite query execution inside traceCallers/traceCallees (all@db-adapter chunk), while traversal logic itself used 10ms.

plannerEvidence.after: SEARCH m USING INDEX brain_symbol_owner_idx (owner_symbol_id>? AND owner_symbol_id<?)

bb_graph_call1_cold.note: first call includes server-side first-open ANALYZE-free path + drizzle init

oneTimeAnalyzeCost.note: paid once at first open (absence-only heal) or as the final post-processing phase; steady state zero

measurements.honestNote: bb_graph cold after fix is ~2.9s vs warm ~0.6s; the residual cold cost is first-open + drizzle warmup in the fresh server process, not the traversal (in-process traversal is 549ms src / 824ms dist). bb_patterns output 'patterns (100): ...' is real content (A1's timeout verdict was pre-fix).

permanentFix.change: ensurePlannerStats(): absence-only heal — if sqlite_stat1 is missing at open, run ANALYZE once (BB_SKIP_ANALYZE=1 escapes); presence costs one sqlite_master lookup.
permanentFix.wiredAt: src/brain/database.ts ensureSchemaIfNew() else-branch (pre-existing DB path, both openDatabase callers) and getInstance()/getRawInstance() via ensureSchemaIfNew

permanentFix.change: ensureHealthIndexes() now also self-heals 8 core traversal indexes (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) and reports recreated count; when an index is actually recreated, stale stat1 rows are rebuilt with a repair-path ANALYZE.
permanentFix.reason: tsx gate run exposed: after DROP INDEX + heal, planner still used stale stat1 referencing the dropped index (plan fell back to SCAN m then project_idx); restore check failed until the repair-path ANALYZE was added

permanentFix.change: runPostProcessing gains an 'analyze' phase (PostProcessingPhaseTiming union extended) — ANALYZE runs unconditionally as the final full post-pass phase so fresh indexes are born with planner stats.

gate.mutation: M1 drops brain_symbol_owner_idx and proves the P3 plan predicate fails (owner_idx disappears from plan) — the gate can fail, so it is a gate
gate.scaleNote: fixture-scale planner heuristics already pick owner_idx without stat1; the stat1 catastrophe is a real-repo-scale phenomenon — the perHop and stdio E2E numbers above are the scale evidence, measured on the real 4.8GB and 816MB DBs

discoveredAndReported: Second data dir: the spawned server resolves BB_DATA_DIR to ~/.khushal_file/.bb (env-injected), while ad-hoc probes assumed ~/.bb — a repo had populated DBs in BOTH. The split was environmental (probe/tooling), not a code defect; no work lost, but it cost a day of confusion. Probe scripts must always record the resolved db path in evidence.
The user's live opencode MCP server (PID 466595, started 00:21) still serves the pre-fix dist; it will pick up the fix on its next restart/rebuild.
mutationChecks: M1 strip stats + drop owner index -> planner full scan
restore: heal recreates the index and re-runs ANALYZE
